key_insight: A single, consistent training recipe lets time-series foundation models reliably improve forecast quality as they scale from 4M to 2.5B parameters; the resulting Toto 2.0 family (five open-weight models) sets new SOTA on multiple benchmarks.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a scalable, reliable approach for building large time-series forecasting models that generalize across domains and remain robust to data contamination.
method: Apply one unified training recipe consistently across model sizes ranging from 4M to 2.5B parameters.
Release a family of five open-weight Toto 2.0 models trained under that recipe to cover a range of compute/latency trade-offs.
Benchmark and validate improvements on three datasets: BOOM (observability), GIFT-Eval (general-purpose), and TIME (contamination-resistant).
impact: Practitioners gain a proven, scalable path to higher-accuracy, more robust forecasting without per-task reengineering; open weights accelerate adoption and reproducibility for production forecasting systems.
visual_elements: Log-scale line chart: forecast error (y) vs model parameters (x) showing steady improvement from 4M to 2.5B
Model family schematic: five Toto 2.0 variants with icons for latency/compute tiers and recommended use-cases
Benchmark bar chart: Toto 2.0 vs prior SOTA across BOOM, GIFT-Eval, and TIME
Robustness heatmap or icon set: contamination-resistance and generalization metrics across domains
paper_title: Toto 2.0: Time Series Forecasting Enters the Scaling Era
paper_authors: Emaad Khwaja, Chris Lettieri, Gerald Woo, Eden Belouadah, Marc Cenac
